comment: Cross-language golden vectors for viewport<->device coordinate mapping (issue #4547, B0 of the
canonical-pixel campaign #4547 -> #4548 -> #4549 -> #4550). This file is the single source of
truth, mirroring test/fixtures/pinch-golden-vectors.json.
Consumers:
- Kotlin: android/desktop-core .../layout/CoordinateMappingGoldenVectorTest.kt holds inline
copies of the five mapper sections and drives DeviceScreenCoordinateMapper against them.
test/parity/coordinateMappingGoldenVectorParity.test.ts parses those inline literals out of
the Kotlin source and verifies them against this file (the pinch drift-guard mechanism).
- TypeScript: test/daemon/deviceDataStreamSocketServer.test.ts drives the daemon's
pixelsMatchClaimedGeometry pairing from the geometryPairing section, and
test/daemon/observationInitialFrame.test.ts drives the daemon's iOS point->pixel conversion
from the iosPointToPixel section, both reading this file directly.
- Swift: ONE consumer, the scaleReporting section. Since #4548 the iOS runner derives the
physical screenshot pixel dimensions it reports (ElementLocator.computePixelDimensions,
points * UIScreen.nativeScale); ElementLocatorTests.swift holds an inline copy of the
scaleReporting rows and the parity suite parses it out of the source. The runner still
performs no viewport<->device mapping: point-space bounds plus screenScale cross the wire
and the point->pixel conversion for geometry pairing happens daemon-side in TypeScript
(IOSCtrlProxyClient.updateScreenGeometryFrom / observationInitialFrame). The runner's other
coordinate math, pinch endpoint geometry, is pinned by pinch-golden-vectors.json.
These vectors PIN CURRENT BEHAVIOR. Rows with willChangeUnderCanonicalPixels=true document
iOS point-space cases whose expected values MUST change when #4549 converts hierarchy bounds
to canonical pixels — a green suite across that change means the conversion silently drifted.
Booleans are encoded as 0/1 so the Kotlin inline tables stay purely numeric for the positional
source parser. In geometryPairing, measuredWidth=measuredHeight=-1 means an unmeasurable frame.
In iosPointToPixel, scale=0 means the hierarchy carried no screenScale (daemon defaults to 1).
scaleReporting (#4548, B1) pins the RUNNER-side derivation of the reported physical pixel
dimensions: pixel = round(point * nativeScale), where nativeScale is UIScreen.nativeScale on
iOS (NOT UIScreen.scale — Display Zoom makes them differ and screenshots render at native
scale) and exactly 1 on Android (bounds are already physical pixels). These rows do NOT carry
willChangeUnderCanonicalPixels: the runner-side derivation is the metadata #4549 consumes and
must stay stable across that change.

viewportToDevice.comment: Android 1080x2340 portrait, frame at half device size: frame center maps to device center
zoom removal: at scale 2 a viewport point twice as far maps to the same device point
pan removal: device origin sits at the pan offset
rounding boundary: viewport 0.25 * ratio 2 = device 0.5, halves round UP to 1
negative rounding boundary: device -0.5 rounds toward positive infinity to 0 (Kotlin roundToInt tie rule)
out of bounds at exactly deviceWidth: bounds are exclusive, no clamping
negative out of bounds: raw negative coordinates are returned, never clamped
x-only negative out of bounds: y well inside — pins the x lower-bound predicate independently (deleting x >= 0 flips only this row)
y-only negative out of bounds: x well inside — pins the y lower-bound predicate independently (deleting y >= 0 flips only this row)
y-only out of bounds: x well inside, y exactly at deviceHeight (exclusive) — pins the y bounds predicate independently of x
far past the bottom-right edge: raw coordinates preserved, flagged out of bounds
landscape device space (rotation-aligned upstream): 2340x1080 with a landscape frame
degenerate zero frame width: frame-to-device ratio falls back to 1 (identity)

iOS 3x device (iPhone-class 390x844): device space is POINTS today, so a 390pt-wide frame maps 1:1. Under #4549 (canonical pixels) deviceWidth/deviceHeight become 1170x2532 and expectedX/expectedY become 585/1266.
iOS 2x device (375x667 points) with fractional viewport input. Under #4549 the device space becomes 750x1334 pixels and the expected coordinates double (modulo rounding).
iOS Display Zoom-like device (320x693 zoomed points at 3x). Under #4549 the device space becomes 960x2079 pixels.

width-derived-ratio invariant: deliberately aspect-MISMATCHED frame (500x500 frame, 1000x2000 device; width ratio 2, height ratio 4). Not a realistic aspect-fitted frame — the pipeline pre-aligns rotation and fits to the device aspect — but it pins the documented rule that BOTH axes scale by deviceWidth/frameWidthPx: a height-derived y would give 800, not 400.

deviceToViewport.comment: inverse of the identity half-frame case: device center back to frame center
inverse with pan + zoom: device (270,585) -> frame (135,292.5) -> viewport (370,635)
degenerate zero device width: device-to-frame ratio falls back to 1 (identity + offset)
iOS 3x point-space inverse. Under #4549 deviceWidth/deviceHeight become 1170x2532 pixels, so the same device point lands at a different viewport position.

width-derived-ratio invariant (inverse): deliberately aspect-MISMATCHED frame (500x500 frame, 1000x2000 device; width ratio 0.5, height ratio 0.25). Not a realistic aspect-fitted frame — it pins the documented rule that BOTH axes scale by frameWidthPx/deviceWidth: a height-derived y would give 100, not 200.

fitToViewport.comment: unknown image width falls back to aspect ratio 2.16 -> height-constrained 340.7407x736
non-default padding 10 (not the 32 default): max sides 780, height-constrained 390x780 — substituting DEFAULT_PADDING would give 368x736
tiny viewport: max frame sides coerce to the 1px floor -> 0.5x1

fitScale.comment: frame fits comfortably: scale caps at 1.0 (never enlarges)
frame far larger than viewport: clamps to the 0.3 floor
mid-range: 736+64=800 padded frame in a 400-wide viewport -> exactly 0.5 (WIDTH candidate decisive)
HEIGHT candidate decisive mid-range: height ratio 400/(736+64)=0.5 binds while the width ratio is 800/(336+64)=2.0 — pins that the height term participates in the min
non-default padding 20 (not the 32 default): padded sides 800, width candidate 400/800=0.5 — substituting DEFAULT_PADDING would give 400/824=0.4854

screenshotRotation.comment: portrait image, portrait bounds: no rotation
landscape image, landscape bounds: no rotation
portrait image, landscape bounds: rotate 90 CW (code 3)
landscape image, portrait bounds: rotate 270 CW (code 1)
non-positive image width: no rotation inferred
non-positive root dimensions: no rotation inferred
iOS pixel screenshot (1170x2532) vs point-space root (390x844): orientations agree across units, so no rotation. Output survives #4549 but the cross-unit comparison it pins does not.
square image counts as landscape (height > width is false) against portrait bounds -> code 1
square ROOT bounds count as landscape against a portrait screenshot -> code 3: pins strict rootHeight > rootWidth (a >= mutation flips this to 0)
DECISIVE zero imageWidth: orientations would MISMATCH (portrait-by-height image, landscape bounds), so deleting the imageWidth guard clause changes the result to 3
DECISIVE zero imageHeight alone: landscape-by-default image vs portrait bounds, so deleting the imageHeight guard clause changes the result to 1
DECISIVE zero rootWidth alone: portrait-by-height bounds vs landscape image, so deleting the rootWidth guard clause changes the result to 1
DECISIVE zero rootHeight alone: landscape-by-default bounds vs portrait image, so deleting the rootHeight guard clause changes the result to 3

geometryPairing.comment: exact match: measured pixels equal the claimed geometry
orientation swap accepted: iOS landscape claim (2532x1170) with native-portrait pixels
aspect-preserving scale change rejected: 720x1560 pixels against a 1080x2340 claim
iOS exact pixel match (claims are already pixel-space today via the daemon's point*scale conversion)
square frame: same-orientation and swapped checks coincide, accepted
single-axis off-by-one rejected: the check is exact, not approximate

ONE-axis swap rejected: measured.width == claimedHeight (1170) but measured.height != claimedWidth (2532 vs 2500) — the swap acceptance is a conjunction, so a frame matching only one opposite axis must never receive a capture identity

iosPointToPixel.comment: 2x device: 375x667 points -> 750x1334 pixels. Under #4549 the hierarchy arrives in canonical pixels and this daemon-side multiply disappears (or becomes identity).
Display Zoom-like: zoomed 320x693 points at 3x -> 960x2079 pixels
fractional scale rounding boundary: 375*2.5 = 937.5 rounds half-up to 938
absent screenScale (0 sentinel): daemon defaults the multiplier to 1

fractional HEIGHT product isolated: 667*2.5 = 1667.5 rounds half-up to 1668 while the width product (400*2.5=1000) is integral — a height-axis-only rounding regression cannot hide behind the width case

scaleReporting.comment: standard 3x device: 393x852 points at nativeScale 3.0 -> 1179x2556 pixels (scale == nativeScale here, so this row alone cannot distinguish them)
Display Zoom: nativeScale 3.144 while UIScreen.scale stays 3.0 — using scale would report 2436, not the screenshot's true 2553 (812*3.144=2552.928 rounds to 2553)
iPhone Plus downsampling panel: scale 3.0 but nativeScale 2.608696 -> the physical 1080x1920
rounding tie on both axes: 375*3.5=1312.5 and 811*3.5=2838.5 round half away from zero (== JS Math.round for positive values)
Android identity contract: bounds are already physical pixels so the runner reports exactly nativeScale 1 with pixel == screen dims
